question: What is the incident of 'Komagata Maru' related to?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian freedom struggle**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Komagata Maru incident** is a significant event in the history of the **Indian freedom struggle**.
 
• It involved a Japanese ship named Komagata Maru, which was hired to transport Indian immigrants to Canada in 1914.
 
• The passengers, mostly Sikhs, were denied entry into Canada due to discriminatory immigration laws, and the ship was forced to return to India.
 
• Upon arrival in India, the British authorities attempted to arrest the passengers, leading to a violent confrontation.
 
• This incident highlighted the racial discrimination faced by Indians abroad and fueled the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Komagata Maru incident took place during the British Raj, a period when India was under British colonial rule.
 
• The incident is often cited as an example of the broader struggles faced by Indian immigrants in the early 20th century.
 
• It also serves as a reminder of the global dimensions of the Indian freedom struggle, influencing not just events in India but also those involving the Indian diaspora.
